note: The only outside opinion this family has left.
Every other check on the loudness chain measures its output with the same
function that decided the gain, which is circular: a wrong BS.1770 would
satisfy all of them. These came from ffmpeg reading files this package wrote.
The tones cover the K-weighting where it is not flat, which is the point of
them: 440 Hz is off 1 kHz, 60 Hz is down the high-pass skirt and 10 kHz is up
on the head shelf. A merely plausible filter passes 1 kHz and fails the ends.
The 60 Hz and 10 kHz tones, the true-peak references and the resampling pair
came from vorlaut's tests/reference/tts.lock.json, which arrived at the same
idea independently and had gone further. Its first three tones and these three
agreed to 0.03 dB before either knew about the other.
Do not re-derive any of this from the code under test - that is the circle it
exists to break. conformance/calibrate.sh regenerates the tones from ffmpeg.
measured_with: ffmpeg ebur128, integrated loudness, on WAV written by encodeWav

tones.why: down the high-pass skirt, the stage the 1 kHz tones do not touch
up on the head shelf; a chain without it reads this one low

note: 4000 Hz at 16 kHz, phase pi/4, so the samples deliberately miss the peaks.
A sine's true peak is exactly its amplitude, so the analytic value is not an
estimate - it is the answer, and it is what a correct chain must approach.

disagreements.what: true peak on a pure sine
why: A sine's true peak is exactly its amplitude. ffmpeg's four-times

Written down because ffmpeg is the oracle everywhere else here, and
the next person to notice this gap will be tempted to close it. Making
the chain agree with ffmpeg would make it wrong, and would cost real
headroom on every recording - a ceiling read 0.55 dB high is a gain
pulled back 0.55 dB further than it needed to be.
disagreements.verdict: ours is right; do not chase agreement

note: 22050 to 16000, which is what a piper medium model needs for a device
that wants 16 kHz. The second case is the one that matters: 10 kHz is
above the 8 kHz Nyquist of the output, so it must vanish rather than
fold down to 6050 Hz and arrive as noise on the consonants.
A threshold rather than a value. vorlaut's ffmpeg-measured pair
reads -62.54 here and ours gates to -Infinity, because ours is
measured after upsampling back to 48 kHz as the contract requires
and there is nothing left to measure. Both are 'gone'; only the
arithmetic of how gone differs, and pinning an exact number would
be pinning that accident.
